why: The new Core Principle (prefer very-early cuts after clause-introducers and make predicate-ending penalties conditional) made the scorer cut earlier around initial clause-introducers, which raised H_set in mid-length bins (≤7 and ≤10) by reducing the previous over-penalization of predicate endings, but caused more harmful very-early splits in short pieces (≤3 and ≤5) that fragment heads/NPs, leaving the overall effect near zero.
lesson: Respect that preferring very-early cuts helps mid-length examples but can hurt very-short pieces by splitting heads/NPs, so later revisions should avoid forcing those very-early cuts in short contexts.
